claim: TubeArchivist uses a cron-like schedule of three values (minute, hour, day-of-week), rejects number/number step syntax in the first field, and enforces a floor of no more than once per hour to avoid YouTube throttling; the Rescan Subscriptions task adds missing videos to the download queue.
quote: Cron format as number/number are non-standard cron formatting and are not supported by the scheduler... the scheduler doesn't support schedules that trigger more than once per hour.

claim: MeTube checks each subscription on a global fixed interval set by SUBSCRIPTION_DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL (default 60 minutes), with SUBSCRIPTION_SCAN_PLAYLIST_END (default 50) capping newest-first entries fetched per check.
quote: SUBSCRIPTION_DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL: Default minutes between automatic checks for each subscription. Defaults to 60.

claim: PinchFlat schedules the next index only after the current one completes (interval-after-completion), so a 60-minute Index Frequency plus a 30-minute index run yields a 90-minute effective cadence; Index Frequency is a per-source field and Fast Indexing (RSS by default, optional API key) speeds detection.
quote: If you set your Media Profile to index every 60 minutes and the indexing task takes 30 minutes to complete, it'll actually run every 90 minutes, since that 60 minute interval was only applied after the indexing task completed.

claim: PinchFlat's API-based fast indexing can poll roughly 65 sources at a 10-minute interval per API key, while RSS fast indexing is the no-key default sufficient for most users.
quote: by default an API key can perform fast indexing for approximately 65 sources with a polling interval of 10 minutes.

claim: ytdl-sub has no internal scheduler; the Docker image's optional cron support runs subscriptions on a user-supplied CRON_SCHEDULE (e.g. "0 */6 * * *" for every 6 hours) with no default, plus CRON_RUN_ON_START to also run at container startup.
quote: Using CRON_RUN_ON_START may cause your cron script to run too often and trigger throttles and bans... it'll run whenever the container starts, including when the host reboots, when dockerd restarts, or when a new image is pulled.

claim: TubeSync sets index frequency per-source (selectable when adding a channel/playlist), runs indexing as background scheduled tasks (Django process_tasks worker), and recommends the longest practical interval up to 24 hours to avoid endlessly re-indexing large channels.
quote: It's a good idea to add sources with as long of an index frequency as possible... it's entirely possible that your TubeSync install may spend its entire time indexing the channel, over and over again, without downloading any media.

claim: YoutubeDL-Material uses a single global check interval (subscriptions_check_interval, default 5 minutes / 300 seconds, stored in config.json) that represents the time to cycle through ALL subscriptions, so per-sub spacing = interval / number of subscriptions rather than a per-channel setting.
quote: The check interval represents the amount of time between cycling through all subscriptions. If you have 10 subscriptions and the interval is set to 100, every 10 seconds another subscription will be checked.

claim: PinchFlat is a self-hosted YouTube media manager that lets users preview which media will be downloaded via a Pending Media tab before downloading, useful for testing filters and shorts/livestream handling.
quote: test your "Title Filter Regex", "Download Cutoff Date", and handling of shorts vs. livestreams ... disable "Download Media" in your Source, and then check the "Pending Media" tab

claim: ytdl-sub's plugins reference documents per-source filtering (date_range before/after, match_filters using yt-dlp expressions to exclude shorts/livestreams) plus SponsorBlock (sponsorblock_categories to embed segment chapters, remove_sponsorblock_categories to cut them) and NFO generation (nfo_tags per entry, output_directory_nfo_tags) for Kodi/Jellyfin/Plex.
quote:
date_range:
  before: "now"
  after: "today-2weeks" ... match_filters:
  filters:
    - "original_url!*=/shorts/ & !is_live"
    - "availability=?public"

claim: ytdl-sub's 'Only Recent' and 'Only Recent Archive' presets use a rolling date_range window (default 2months) via only_recent_date_range, and 'Only Recent' additionally deletes files outside the window using keep_files_after, with keep_max_files available for a fixed file cap.
quote: after parameter set to "today-{only_recent_date_range}" ... default duration is "2months" ... 'Only Recent' ... implements keep_files_after: "today-{only_recent_date_range}" to remove older content ... keep_max_files override defaults to 0

claim: TubeArchivist controls per-channel content type via Video Page Size, Live Page Size, and Shorts Page Size; setting Live or Shorts page size to 0 disables indexing/downloading those types for a channel.
quote: Live Page Size: Same as above, but for a channel's live streams. Disable by setting to 0. Shorts Page Size: Same as above, but for a channel's shorts videos. Disable by setting to 0.

claim: TubeArchivist supports Page Size Overrides per channel (setting a value to 0 deactivates shorts for that channel) but offers no title-regex, date-cutoff, or duration download filter; it relies on page-size caps and Auto Delete Watched for retention.
quote: overwrite the page size per channel ... by setting a value to 0 (zero) you can effectively deactivate shorts on this channel, for example

claim: TubeSync Source model exposes filter_text (regex on video titles), filter_text_invert (skip matching titles), filter_seconds with filter_seconds_min (min/max duration), source_resolution (desired resolution), and days_to_keep/delete_old_media for retention.
quote: filter_text: Regex compatible filter string for video titles ... filter_text_invert: Invert filter string regex match, skip any matching titles ... filter_seconds: Filter Media based on Min/Max duration ... filter_seconds_min ... skip on minimum ... or maximum ... days_to_keep ... delete_old_media

claim: TubeSync's keyword and duration source filters originated as feature request issue #266, asking to exclude media on a source by keyword or by length.
quote: Allow exclusion of media on a source by keyword or by length (to not download media under a certain length).

claim: Every public YouTube channel exposes a free RSS feed at videos.xml?channel_id=UC..., but the raw feed only ever returns the 15 most recent uploads.
quote: The raw feed shows 15 videos at a time. YouTube's RSS feed only contains the 15 most recent uploads at any given moment.

claim: The 15-video cap on the channel RSS feed is a hard YouTube limit that third-party services work around to surface more history.
quote: BUT only the most recent 15 videos will be listed!

claim: Native YouTube RSS only shows a handful of recent videos while a channel may have hundreds, so workaround services expand the window up to ~1000 items.
quote: YouTube channels could have hundreds of videos, but only the most recent 10 videos will show up in your feed.

claim: YouTube RSS feeds have propagation latency: a new video can take up to an hour after the WebSub push to actually appear in the feed, and YouTube's WebSub posts are not spec-compliant so they only serve as a re-fetch ping.
quote: YouTube often sends notifications before the entries appear in the feed... up to an hour after the WebSub push... YouTube WebSub posts are not spec compliant and do not contain the required information to send notifications.

claim: yt-dlp's --download-archive records the IDs of downloaded videos and downloads only videos not listed in it; --break-on-existing stops the run on the first archived file; --break-per-input scopes that break (and --max-downloads / --break-match-filters) to each input URL; --flat-playlist lists entries without extracting them.
quote: Download only videos not listed in the archive file... Stop the download process when encountering a file that is in the archive supplied with the --download-archive option... Alters --max-downloads, --break-on-existing, --break-match-filters, and autonumber to reset per input URL

claim: There is a known inconsistency where, with --break-per-input enabled, --break-on-existing breaks per input URL rather than per playlist, introduced by PR #5439.
quote: Inconsistency between `--break-on-existing` and `--playlist-end` with `--break-per-input` enabled

claim: yt-dlp is the dominant extraction engine these tools wrap, with roughly 169k GitHub stars as of June 2026.
quote: Star 169k

claim: --flat-playlist is used to index a channel/playlist by listing all entries (URLs/IDs/metadata) without downloading, e.g. yt-dlp --flat-playlist --print id, making it the heavier-but-complete alternative to RSS for enumerating an entire channel.
quote: yt-dlp --flat-playlist --print url PLAYLIST_URL to list all video URLs without downloading... --flat-playlist --dump-json to get full metadata without downloading

claim: TubeArchivist advises a ~3s sleep interval between YouTube requests to avoid throttling, a 90-day refresh window to spread requests, and notes residential IPs can get throttled (a shared proxy/VPN IP may help).
quote: Sleep Interval: Time in seconds to sleep between requests to YouTube. It's a good idea to set this to 3 seconds... some users have reported throttling issues from residential IP address ranges. You might be able to avoid that with a shared IP from a Proxy/VPN.

claim: In Feb 2026 (yt-dlp stable 2026.02.04) a wave hit where all public, login-free YouTube videos began returning LOGIN_REQUIRED 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot', with the error itself suggesting cookies, updating to nightly/master, and PO tokens.
quote: Sign in to confirm you're not a bot. Use --cookies-from-browser or --cookies for the authentication... LOGIN_REQUIRED status [across web, web_safari, android_vr]

claim: PO Tokens (proof-of-origin) are generated by BotGuard/DroidGuard/iOSGuard, are bound to the video/session and expire fast, and YouTube continuously updates enforcement so the guidance is provisional.
quote: PO Tokens are still an active area of research, and YouTube is continuously updating the implementation and enforcement... A PO Token is generated by either BotGuard (Web), DroidGuard (Android), or iOSGuard (iOS), and a PO Token from one platform cannot be used on another.

claim: The bgutil POT provider runs alongside yt-dlp (preferably as an always-running HTTP server with a prebuilt Docker image) to generate PO tokens on demand, which yt-dlp picks up automatically; HTTP-server mode is recommended for production with repeated requests.
quote: What works is a small helper called bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider running on the side; it generates tokens on demand and the main yt-dlp call picks them up automatically... HTTP server mode is recommended for production deployments with multiple requests.

claim: Providing a PO token does not guarantee bypassing 403/bot checks but makes traffic appear more legitimate; install via pip as a yt-dlp plugin.
quote: Providing a PO token does not guarantee bypassing 403 errors or bot checks, but it may help your traffic seem more legitimate.

claim: yt-dlp's cookie-export guidance exists precisely because YouTube rotates and invalidates cookies on continued browser use: export from a fresh private/incognito window, then close it so the session is never reopened, otherwise the cookies are invalidated.
quote: Open a new private browsing/incognito window and log into YouTube... Export youtube.com cookies from the browser... Close the private browsing/incognito window so that the session is never opened in the browser again.

claim: Users report that authenticating yt-dlp with browser cookies carries account ban risk (temporary or permanent), motivating throwaway accounts and caution on request rate/volume.
quote: Question about risk of using cookies-from-browser... whether YouTube permanently bans accounts for using cookies with yt-dlp [and] whether cookies remain valid when used outside the browser

claim: PinchFlat lists Apprise notifications, SponsorBlock integration, first-class Plex/Jellyfin/Kodi metadata support, podcast RSS feeds, and custom post-download/delete scripts as features.
quote: Apprise support for notifications ... Sponsorblock integration ... First-class support for media center apps like Plex, Jellyfin, and Kodi ... Supports serving RSS feeds to your favourite podcast app ... [Advanced] supports running custom scripts when after downloading/deleting media (alpha

claim: PinchFlat runs a single lifecycle script at <config>/extras/user-scripts/lifecycle, called with an event type plus JSON data, for events app_init, media_pre_download, media_downloaded, and media_deleted (bash or Python 3, jq bundled).
quote: a file is created at <pinchflat config directory>/extras/user-scripts/lifecycle ... called with 2 arguments: the event type and a JSON representation ... events - app_init, media_pre_download, media_downloaded, and media_deleted ... use bash or Python 3. jq has been installed in the container

claim: A separate Jellyfin plugin maps TubeArchivist's SponsorBlock data into Jellyfin's Media Segments feature via a Media Segment Scan task, requiring both it and the existing TubeArchivist Jellyfin metadata plugin to be installed.
quote: This Jellyfin plugin integrates the Sponsorblock functionality of Tube Archivist with Jellyfin's Media Segments feature ... This plugin does not implement the metadata provider functionality of the existing TubeArchivist Jellyfin plugin ... you need both installed

claim: PinchFlat users request a configurable delay between a video being discovered/indexed and downloaded so SponsorBlock crowd-sourced segments have time to aggregate, indicating SponsorBlock data quality depends on download timing.
quote: Wait # days/hours before downloading a video after discovering the video following indexing to allow SponsorBlock to aggregate.

claim: ChannelTube (~314 stars, last release v0.9.3 May 2026) is a Docker web-UI tool that fetches new YouTube channel content on a yt-dlp schedule defined by a comma-separated list of hours, with optional Plex/Jellyfin library-scan triggers.
quote: Download Video or Audio from YouTube channels on a schedule via yt-dlp. ... a comma-separated list of hours to search for new items

claim: Subarr (~405 stars, v1.2 Dec 2025) is a lightweight 'Sonarr for YouTube' that polls RSS feeds every ~15 minutes but is explicitly limited to the last 15 feed items and can miss videos when many uploads occur rapidly.
quote: Limited to the last 15 items in feeds ... Won't function properly for playlists with 15+ items ... May miss videos if many uploads occur rapidly ... works perfectly fine for mine

claim: Youtarr (~1.2k stars, v1.70.0 May 30 2026) is a yt-dlp-powered web app that subscribes to channels and auto-downloads new videos/shorts/streams on a cron-based schedule with per-tab controls and optional Plex/Kodi/Jellyfin/Emby integration.
quote: Subscribe to channels and auto-download new videos, shorts, and streams with per-tab controls ... Scheduled Downloads: Configure automatic downloads on your schedule (cron-based)

claim: A TubeSync GitHub issue reports all video downloads stalling, one of several open reliability reports (alongside skipped/stuck downloads) about its channel-watching pipeline.
quote: All video downloads stalled

claim: TubeSync users hit large batches of videos marked 'skipped' and requested a batch-restart feature, indicating individual retrying is otherwise tedious when many uploads are missed.
quote: request: ability to batch restart skipped downloads

claim: The simplest DIY channel watcher is `yt-dlp --download-archive watched.txt <channel/playlist URL>` run periodically via cron, which records downloaded video IDs and skips them on later runs so only new uploads are grabbed.
quote: yt-dlp --download-archive watched.txt "https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=..." ... Run this command periodically (via cron job or Task Scheduler) to automatically grab new uploads.

claim: ytdl-sub (~2.8k stars, release 2026.05.10) is a YAML-subscription wrapper around yt-dlp that automates channel downloads and metadata for Plex/Jellyfin/Kodi, scheduled via cron or its Docker CRON_SCHEDULE env var rather than a web UI.
quote: Lightweight tool to automate downloading and metadata generation with yt-dlp

claim: A 2025 Hacker News thread captures the recurring demand for an '*arr style app' that keeps a list of YouTube channels archived indefinitely, with commenters recommending Youtarr, TubeArchivist (good Jellyfin integration) and RSS-based scripts as answers.
quote: an *arr style app that I can give a list of Youtube channels I want archived, and it would just keep the archive up to date indefinitely
